guard: an agent's DM send ACL is exactly the owners named in allowDmOwners, with omitted meaning the historical wildcard and empty meaning no DM at all, and narrowing it moves no other grant
why: The DM grant was a hardcoded `inst.*.*.<owner>.<actor>`: every agent on a space could DM every
other agent, and no deployment could confine one tenant's agents to its own people. The option
that narrows it is DEFAULT-ALLOW, which is the opposite reflex to the post ACL two lines above,
so the two mistakes that matter pull in opposite directions and neither is visible in a diff.
E1 flips the default to deny. That is the change a default-deny reflex makes, it reads as a
hardening, and it would cut the DM plane of every existing space on upgrade — the one outcome
this option exists to avoid. E4 is the same collapse from the other side and is the likelier of
the two to be written by hand: `?.length ? … : ["*"]` is the ordinary empty-guard idiom, it
leaves the omitted case correct so most cells stay green, and it silently converts an explicit
'this agent sends no DMs' into 'this agent DMs anyone'. E1 and E4 are both needed because each
one alone is survivable by a suite that only tests the other direction.
E2 restores the historical hardcode with the option still parsed and unused, which is what a
revert or a bad merge produces. E3 keeps the narrowing but pins the recipient ACTOR slot, which
over-narrows: the DM would reach only a recipient whose actor name happened to equal the
sender's, so an in-policy DM to a real teammate silently stops arriving.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports core by relative source path (../src/index.js) and runs
under tsx, so the mutated file is the file that executes and no build step stands between them.
The cells that grade the mutants are broker verdicts from a real nats-server auth callout, not a
restatement of the rule in the test: a mutation that changes the emitted grant changes what the
broker answers, which is the only thing the cells read.
NOT COVERED HERE, deliberately: the auth ledger's resolver, which carries allowDmOwners from a
stored row into this mint. This suite calls mintCreds directly, so a resolver that drops the
field leaves every cell below green. That seam is graded where it lives, not here.

mutations.name: E1 omitted collapses to DENY (the default-deny reflex)
mutations.expectRed: ABSENT ⇒ the historical wildcard: DM owner C ALLOWED TOO (no narrowing on upgrade)
mutations.cell: ABSENT ⇒ the historical wildcard: DM owner C ALLOWED TOO (no narrowing on upgrade)
mutations.note: Mutates the default only. Every explicitly-scoped cell above stays green, so the kill can come from nothing but the upgrade-path cell this option exists to protect.

mutations.name: E2 the historical hardcode returns; the option is parsed and ignored
mutations.expectRed: DM an OUT-OF-POLICY owner DENIED (the whole point)
mutations.cell: DM an OUT-OF-POLICY owner DENIED (the whole point)
mutations.note: `dmOwners` stays declared and stays type-correct, so neither the compiler nor a reader of the surrounding lines sees anything missing — the shape a revert or a bad three-way merge leaves behind.

mutations.name: E3 the recipient ACTOR slot is pinned instead of wildcard (over-narrowing)
mutations.expectRed: the recipient ACTOR slot stays a WILDCARD — a SECOND actor of the same owner is ALLOWED
mutations.cell: the recipient ACTOR slot stays a WILDCARD — a SECOND actor of the same owner is ALLOWED
mutations.note: The out-of-policy cell still passes under this mutant, so it cannot be what kills it: over-narrowing is a distinct defect from under-narrowing and needs its own cell to be visible at all.

mutations.name: E4 EMPTY silently re-widens to the wildcard (the empty-guard idiom)
mutations.expectRed: EMPTY ⇒ no DM send at all: owner C DENIED
mutations.cell: EMPTY ⇒ no DM send at all: owner C DENIED
mutations.note: The omitted case stays correct under this mutant and E1's cell stays green, which is exactly why E1 cannot stand in for it: this is the collapse that survives a suite testing only the upgrade direction.
